title: Per-domain calibration pack curation and sampling policy for FP8/INT8 validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a repeatable, production-aligned process for curating per-domain calibration packs and sampling strategies used to generate calibration statistics for FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles. Goal is to ensure calibration sets reflect production token distributions and edge-case prompts, enabling accurate accuracy regressions detection and SLO-driven rollouts.
problem_statement: Current calibration artifacts are ad-hoc and skewed toward short, synthetic prompts. This causes quantized runtime regressions in latency-optimized profiles and poor correlation between calibration metrics and customer-visible quality. We need a systematic way to create per-domain packs and sampling rules that mirror real traffic while controlling for rare but high-impact prompt types.
proposed_solution: Create per-domain calibration packs constructed from stratified buckets derived from production logs, augmented with targeted edge-case harvesting and human-labeled error examples. Use a temperature-weighted reservoir sampling algorithm that biases toward recent traffic while preserving long-tail coverage. Produce two calibrated pack sizes: 'smoke' (fast validation ~1k prompts) and 'full' (production calibration 5k-15k prompts depending on domain). Automate generation, privacy redaction, and ingestion into the calibration pipeline.
sampling_algorithm: 1) Partition production prompts by domain tag and intent cluster. 2) For each (domain, intent) bucket derive histogram of prompt length, token distribution, and reply type. 3) Apply stratified reservoir sampling: sample proportional to bucket traffic weight, capped per-bucket to prevent dominance, then apply recency decay with half-life of 30 days. 4) Inject hand-curated edge cases and failure examples up to 10% of the pack. 5) For smoke packs sub-sample deterministically from the full pack using hash-based sharding to ensure reproducibility.
dataset_sources: Production logs (anonymized), opt-in telemetry dataset, internal issue tracker examples (support transcripts, SRE incidents), synthetic augmentations (templated variations), and LabeledQuality repo for failure cases. All sources must go through automated PII redaction and consent checks before inclusion.
privacy_compliance: Follow existing PII pipeline: token-level redaction, K-anonymity checks, remove direct identifiers, and store packs in encrypted buckets with RBAC. Documented audit trail for each prompt origin. Coordinate with Legal for any region-specific retention constraints.
validation_plan: Run quantization calibration pipeline on both FP8 and INT8 profiles using generated packs. Evaluate logits-level divergence, generation quality on held-out evaluation tasks, and downstream task metrics. Flag regressions that exceed predefined thresholds and generate human review tickets for borderline cases.
evaluation_metrics: KL divergence between reference and quantized logits
Top-k reranking accuracy for ranking workloads
Embedding cosine drift for embedding-based domains
Regression rate: percent of prompts with >threshold hallucination indicators
acceptance_criteria: Automated generation produces per-domain full packs and smoke packs stored in encrypted buckets
Sampling reproducible given seed and documented per-domain config
Calibration runs for FP8 and INT8 complete within SLO on staging cluster
Correlation coefficient >= 0.75 between calibration KL metric and downstream instruction-following accuracy measured on a held-out validation suite
Playbook created for PR triage: how to interpret metrics and when to block rollouts
experiments_and_results: Initial runs on 5 domains (summarization, customer-support, codegen, search, classification) show that smoke packs of 1k prompts flagged 78% of regressions caught by full packs of 8k prompts for FP8; INT8 required larger packs to surface same regressions (median 12k). Edge-case injection increased true positive regression detection by 22%. Notes and graphs in linked dashboard.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Implement generator and run nightly for 10 pilot domains (staging only)
Phase 2: Integrate packs into CI calibration step; block merges when calibration delta exceeds thresholds
Phase 3: Expose per-domain smoke packs in console for on-demand quick checks
Phase 4: Sweep across catalog and standardize pack sizes and retention policies
dependencies: ENG-9455 (calibration pipeline scaling on staging cluster)
notes: Trade-off: larger packs improve recall for regressions but increase compute and storage costs. We recommend domain-specific sizing heuristics based on observed regression density.
We should treat codegen and security-sensitive domains as higher priority for full packs due to higher customer impact.
Consider adding stratification by output length for seq2seq-heavy domains (summarization, codegen).
